obligation: G122 -- per-route ns and bytes reconciling to TOKEN_NS and DRAM bytes/token
the_two_axes_reconcile_very_differently: BYTES close to 0.0285% -- the per-route element census times the codec width accounts for essentially all DRAM traffic, because bytes ARE routes: every byte moved is a weight some route reads. NS leave a 25.5% residual, because time is not only weight movement -- norms, rope, softmax and the recurrent state update all consume it and belong to no single route's weight stream. The asymmetry is the finding: a route graph explains the artifact completely and the clock only three-quarters.
the_residual_is_the_same_one: 7.772 ms here against G108's 7.837 and G093's 7.949 from the dispatch side. Three decompositions on three different observables, one term.
what_is_derived_not_measured: per-route ns and bytes are DERIVED: the element census divided by route count, priced at the measured 0.8425 ps/element and the declared 4.25 bits. Exact in aggregate because both inputs are measured, but it apportions elements evenly across layers of a kind. The residual is not apportioned at all -- per-kernel timing to split it does not exist in this runtime.
